insights.headline: MCX gold and silver steady near one-year lows as the dollar holds a 19-month high
insights.summary: MCX December gold held near ₹1,35,000 per 10 g and silver near ₹1,70,000 per kg on Tuesday after Monday’s slide to one-year lows, with spot gold near $3,857. Markets price a 96.6% chance of a December Fed hike as the dollar sits at a 19-month high and the 10-year Treasury yield tops 5%, putting gold on course for its worst year since 2015. Goldman Sachs cut its end-2027 gold call to $4,650, while jewellers reported record Dhanteras sales and wedding-season demand stays in focus.
points: MCX December gold rose 0.59% to an intraday high of ₹1,35,341 per 10 g on Tuesday, from a previous close of ₹1,34,539.
MCX December silver jumped 1.8%, or ₹3,162, to ₹1,71,025 per kg on Tuesday.
Spot gold was little changed near $3,857 early on Tuesday after hitting its lowest since October 2025 on Monday.
Markets see a 96.6% chance of a 25-basis-point December Fed hike, with a 3.4% chance of a 50-point move.
Goldman Sachs cut its end-2027 gold forecast to $4,650 an ounce from $4,800, citing further Fed hikes and soft private demand.

brief.headline: Gold steadies after Monday's slide; dollar stays firm
brief.summary: MCX gold rose to ₹1,35,341 per 10 g and silver to ₹1,71,025 per kg on Tuesday as spot gold held near $3,857.

bullets.text: Gold and silver steadied in Tuesday trade after Monday's slide to one-year lows, with silver recovering more sharply than gold on MCX.
A 19-month-high dollar, 10-year yields above 5% and near-certain December Fed hike bets kept bullion pinned, Reuters says.
Watch tonight: US retail sales and import prices are due at 19:00 IST, ahead of Wednesday's Fed meeting minutes.

trending.title: Gold and silver steady after Monday's slide
trending.summary: Tuesday's session opened with a steadying on MCX after Monday's rout to one-year lows, helped by a softer dollar and safe-haven buying, though both metals remain near their lows.

trending.title: Fed hike bets and a 19-month-high dollar cap bullion
trending.summary: A 19-month-high dollar and a near-certain December Fed hike keep bullion under pressure, with gold on course for its worst year in more than a decade.

trending.title: Silver demand softens even as supply stays short
trending.summary: Silver has fallen further than gold from its record, hit by ETF outflows and softer industrial demand, even as solar demand and a $50 floor draw attention.

trending.title: Festive demand holds up as jewellers report records
trending.summary: Record Dhanteras sales and a 34% jump in October gems exports, even as Indian gold buying fell 29% last quarter; the World Gold Council says festive buying was healthy.

trending.title: Foreign gold at the New York Fed hits a seven-decade low
trending.summary: Gold held for foreign governments at the New York Fed is at its smallest since 1957, as central banks spread custody risk away from the US.

items.title: Gold price today, Nov 17: MCX Gold rises to ₹1,35,341/10 grams, silver jumps ₹3,162/kg; why are prices rising today?
items.summary: MCX December gold rose 0.59% to an intraday high of ₹1,35,341 per 10 g on Tuesday morning, from a previous close of ₹1,34,539, while December silver jumped 1.8%, or ₹3,162, to ₹1,71,025 per kg. Upstox attributes the rebound to safe-haven buying and a marginal pullback in the US dollar after Monday's slide to one-year lows.

items.title: Gold hovers near over one-year low as firm dollar, Fed-hike bets weigh
items.summary: Spot gold was little changed at $3,856.52 an ounce early on Tuesday, staying near its lowest since October 2025 after Monday's slide, putting bullion on course for its worst year in more than a decade. Markets see a 96.6% chance of a 25-basis-point Fed hike in December and await the minutes of the Fed's October 27-28 meeting due on Wednesday. Spot silver steadied at $47.05 an ounce.

items.title: Gold Stays Fragile Below 4,000 as US Dollar Strength and Rate-Hike Bets Weigh
items.summary: Gold tried to steady near $3,870 on Tuesday after sliding to its lowest since October 2025, following a near-4.6% fall last week and a retreat from the $4,150 area, Investing.com reports. A dollar near 19-month highs and a December Fed hike now almost fully priced in kept bullion pinned, while investors await Wednesday's FOMC minutes; Middle East uncertainty underpinned the dollar.

items.title: Gold (XAUUSD) & Silver Price Forecast: Gold Hovers Near One-Year Low on Fed Hike Bets, Can $3,832 Hold?
items.summary: Spot gold steadied near $3,857 on Tuesday after Monday's slide to a one-year low near $3,830, with buyers defending the $3,832 support while $3,888 caps the bounce, FXEmpire notes; silver steadied near $47.05 after Monday's 3.6% drop.

items.title: Gold prices near 1-year low, silver slides as dollar hits 19-month high
items.summary: Gold and silver steadied on Tuesday after Monday's sell-off but stayed near their lowest in more than a year, with spot gold at $3,856.52 an ounce and silver up 0.3% at $47.17. MCX gold closed around ₹1,34,550 per 10 g and silver at ₹1,68,001 per kg. A 19-month-high dollar, 10-year yields near 5.15% and a 96.6% chance of a December Fed hike kept bullion under pressure.

items.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD picks up to $47.50 but remains near yearly lows
items.summary: Silver steadied near $47.50 on Tuesday after bouncing from a yearly low of $46.56, FXStreet notes, with the rebound capped by a firm dollar and elevated Treasury yields as markets price a December Fed hike and more tightening in early 2027; the broader bearish trend stays intact, with silver still well below its late-August peak near $71.

items.title: Foreign Gold in New York Fed Hits 7-Decade Low
items.summary: Foreign governments and central banks now hold the least gold at the New York Fed since 1957, BullionVault reports, as central banks spread custody risk away from the US; France sold its New York holdings and the Netherlands moved bars to London, while the share of central banks keeping any gold at the Fed fell to 14%.

items.title: Gold and Silver Alert: Is a Precious Metals Reversal Ahead?
items.summary: Investing.com asks whether Tuesday's steadier start can turn into a reversal after Monday's slide took gold to a one-year low near $3,830 and silver down 3.6%, with traders watching US retail sales due later today for the next cue.

items.title: Goldman forecasts gold price to take two years to recapture all-time highs
items.summary: Goldman Sachs expects gold to stay volatile in the near term as the Federal Reserve keeps raising rates, but sees prices grinding higher to $4,650 an ounce by end-2027 on continued central-bank buying of about 60 tonnes a month. The bank expects Western ETF demand to recover once the Fed starts cutting rates, supporting a rally to $5,600 by end-2028.

items.title: India gold market update: Gold demand gets festive boost
items.summary: The World Gold Council says festive demand was healthy across regions in jewellery and bars and coins, helped by softer prices; Indian gold ETFs saw a fifth straight month of net inflows in October at Rs 35bn, imports rebounded to a six-month high, and domestic discounts narrowed to $5/oz by 12 November.

items.title: Silver Price Forecast: Slide Continues as Dollar Strengthens
items.summary: FXEmpire's silver outlook stays downbeat: with the dollar strong and Treasury yields rising, spot silver has no durable bottom until the dollar tops, it says; the $46.48-$45.55 zone is the next test, with the 52-week moving average at $68.98 as resistance.

items.title: Gold, Silver Hits 1-Year Low Amid Dollar Rally; Should You Buy Before Wedding Season?
items.summary: Gold and silver stayed under pressure on Tuesday after Monday's slide, with spot gold near $3,857 and silver near $47.17; MCX December gold settled near ₹1,34,550 per 10 g on Monday and silver near ₹1,68,001 per kg, with wedding-season demand in focus as prices sit near one-year lows.

items.title: Why Silver rates crashed from record high of ₹4 lakh per kg price to below ₹1.75 lakh? Experts explain 3 key reasons
items.summary: Silver has plunged nearly 60% from its January record above ₹4 lakh per kg to below ₹1.75 lakh, Mint reports. MCX December silver traded around ₹1,70,065 per kg on Tuesday, up 1.3% from Monday's close, after COMEX silver hit a fresh 52-week low near $47.22 an ounce. Experts blame forced selling and margin calls, a roughly 5% fall in demand, further US rate hike expectations and a stronger dollar.

items.title: Gold down 23%, silver plunges 55%: Why precious metals are losing their shine
items.summary: Gold has fallen more than 23% from its January peak of about ₹1.80 lakh per 10 g to around ₹1.37 lakh, while silver is nearly 55% below its record ₹4.20 lakh per kg, Fortune India reports. A strong dollar, Treasury yields above 5% and rising bets on a December Fed hike have driven the sell-off; the report puts spot-gold support at $3,850 and silver support at $47.

items.title: Gold falls to Rs 1.33 lakh, silver under Rs 1.70 lakh as sell-off deepens in precious metal prices
items.summary: Gold has fallen 5.7% since November 9 to Rs 1,33,797 per 10 g and silver 8.8% to Rs 1,69,591 per kg, with global gold near $3,800 an ounce and silver near $47, both one-year lows, as a strong dollar, rising Treasury yields and 92% odds of a December Fed hike weigh on bullion.

items.title: Silver prices crash by Rs 7,000; dollar strength, rate hike prospects weigh
items.summary: Silver fell Rs 7,115 per kg to Rs 1,69,194 on MCX as the dollar index hovered near a 19-month high around 103.44. Stronger-than-expected US inflation, with consumer prices up 0.4% in October, has investors pricing in a higher chance of further Fed rate rises, while rising Treasury yields lift the cost of holding silver.

items.title: Silver ETFs Crash 5%: What's The Bearish Demand Forecast That Triggered Selloff
items.summary: Silver ETFs fell nearly 5%, with the SBI Silver ETF down 4.76% to Rs 165.20 in its biggest fall since September 26, after Metals Focus forecast global silver demand down 5% in 2026, with jewellery demand contracting about 5% even as industrial demand is set to rise 1% to a record 710 million ounces.

items.title: Gold price slides as Fed hike bets rise, silver bar and coin sales drop despite lower prices – Heraeus
items.summary: Gold fell back below $4,000 an ounce after October CPI rose 0.4% month on month, above the 0.3% expected, with core inflation up 0.3% for a third month. Heraeus notes a 25-basis-point December hike is now fully expected, with about a 10% chance of a 50-point move. Silver dropped below $47, and Perth Mint silver sales fell 36% in October despite the lower price.

items.title: 'Plenty of Reasons to Sell' as Gold Sinks 15% in 12 Weeks
items.summary: Gold has fallen 15.1% over the 12 weeks to 13 November, its fifth-steepest 12-week drop in 20 years and the most persistent of the five, with prices down in 10 of the 12 weeks. Spot gold slid to $3,833 early on Monday, a 13-month low, as US rate-hike expectations held the 10-year Treasury yield above 5% and the dollar near its strongest since April 2025.

items.title: From Above Rs 4 Lakh To Below Rs 1.75 Lakh: Why Silver Prices Have Fallen So Sharply
items.summary: MCX silver has fallen nearly 60% from the Rs 4 lakh per kg peak first breached in January to Rs 1.69 lakh, with COMEX silver at a new 52-week low near $47.22 an ounce. A stronger dollar, elevated bond yields, ETF outflows and weaker industrial demand, including slower AI and solar demand, are behind the slide, analysts say.

items.title: India bought 29% less gold last quarter. So how did Titan and Kalyan grow over 20%?
items.summary: India's gold demand fell 29% by weight to 162.5 tonnes in July-September as record prices curbed buying, the World Gold Council said, yet Titan's domestic jewellery revenue rose 21% and Kalyan's India revenue 27% as higher prices lifted sales value. Titan's profit more than doubled to Rs 2,393 crore and Kalyan's rose 64%, helped by recycled gold and lighter jewellery.

items.title: Senco Gold reports record ₹2,426 crore Dhanteras sales, up 26%; retail revenue rises 25%
items.summary: Senco Gold posted record festive-season retail sales of over ₹2,426 crore between 1 October and 11 November, up 26% on last year, despite volatile and elevated gold prices. Retail revenue rose 25%, and the jeweller crossed ₹10,000 crore in sales on a trailing 12-month basis. The company credited higher footfalls, new customers and its Dhanteras campaign.

items.title: Silver prices find $50 floor as solar industry seeks to accelerate shift toward copper
items.summary: Metals Focus sees silver holding a floor near $50 an ounce after its retreat from January's record $121.65, though it warns prices can still dip below that level. The Silver Institute and Metals Focus expect a sixth straight annual deficit in 2026, with demand beating supply by 35 million ounces, while solar makers speed a shift to copper to cut silver use.

items.title: Silver leads Gold to new 2026 lows: What the ratio says
items.summary: December gold futures traded near $3,880 after sliding to $3,835.20, their lowest since September 19, 2025, while December silver traded near $47 after touching $46.885, its lowest since September 25, 2025. Silver fell faster than gold, pushing the gold-to-silver ratio to about 82.7, its highest since November 2025. The slide is attributed to hawkish Fed talk and a dollar index at new 2026 highs.

items.title: Rupee rises 27 paise to close at 93.92 against US dollar
items.summary: The rupee rose 27 paise to close at 93.92 per dollar on Monday, snapping a two-day decline, as foreign fund inflows, a rally in domestic equities and softer crude oil prices supported the currency. Foreign investors have bought nearly $10 billion of Indian shares in November, while the dollar index stayed near a 19-month high at 103.44.

items.title: India's Jewelry Exports Surge 34% in October
items.summary: India's gem and jewellery exports jumped 34% year on year to $2.92 billion in October, GJEPC data shows, with gold jewellery exports up 48.2% to $1.26 billion, studded gold jewellery up 67.3% and silver jewellery up 55.5%; GJEPC cautioned the gain was flattered by last October's Diwali factory shutdowns and higher gold prices, and expects about 10% export growth in FY27.

items.title: Gold prices boost jewellers' sales, but profits tell a mixed story
items.summary: Record gold prices lifted jewellers' revenues but squeezed margins in the September quarter: Thangamayil's revenue rose 40% to Rs 2,381 crore while profit was flat, Titan's jewellery margin was 11.1% after a Rs 490 crore customs-duty gain, and Kalyan's profit rose 64% to Rs 427 crore. Titan is expanding 18-carat jewellery and Kalyan sees more exchange-led purchases.

items.title: Planning to buy wedding gold in Dubai? Women get higher duty-free limits than men: Customs rules explained
items.summary: Dubai gold looks cheaper than Delhi - 24k at about Rs 11,872 a gram against about Rs 13,620 in Delhi - but Indian customs duty-free limits cover jewellery only: 40 g for women and 20 g for men, with 15% duty above the allowance, the Economic Times explains.

items.title: Gold hallmarking: CAG flags inspection gaps at jewellery shops; experts share 5 checks buyers should know
items.summary: A draft CAG audit has flagged weak oversight of hallmarked gold jewellery, finding BIS inspected only 5,444 of 28,865 licensed jewellers in 2024-25, with over 81% going unchecked over five years, and missing 43.7% of its surveillance target for hallmarking centres; the findings raise questions over purity assurance for buyers, and the report is expected to be tabled in Parliament.

items.title: US dollar hits 19-month peak on Fed hike bets; Aussie dips
items.summary: The dollar index rose to 103.66 on Tuesday, its highest since April 2025 and a sixth straight daily gain, as traders now see a December Fed hike as a certainty, with only around 4% odds on a half-point move. The euro slipped to a 19-month low of $1.0985 and the Aussie to its lowest since January. US retail sales due later on Tuesday could offer further clues on the Fed's path.
